newsitem.title: THAILAND: Cambodians flee to Thailand as fighting flares.
newsitem.headline: Cambodians flee to Thailand as fighting flares.

text.p: Factional fighting broke out on Friday in northwestern Cambodia, forcing thousands of refugees to flee across the frontier into this Thai border town, witnesses said.
The shelling and small arms fire began early as forces loyal to Cambodian strongman Hun Sen attacked those of ousted premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh, refugees said.

The casualty count was not clear, as the refugees said they fled as soon as they heard the fighting in O'Bei Choan, about 30 km (18 miles) northeast of the Cambodian trading town of Poipet. Some refugees came from another neighbouring village.
One woman from O'Bei Choan gave birth shortly after crossing into Thailand, refugees said.
Military officials in Phnom Penh said they had not heard about the fighting but said there had been small clashes in the Poipet area, which lies near the Thai-Cambodian border, in recent days.
Sporadic gunfire could be heard through the day in this town in Aranyaprathet district in eastern Thailand after about 5,000-6,000 refugees fled across the border.
Thai military officials on the border said later on Friday that Hun Sen's forces had captured O'Bei Choan and its 200 royalist defenders had withdrawn into the bush.

Friday's movement of refugees was the first time Cambodians had been allowed across the border en masse since before U.N.-sponsored elections in Cambodia in 1993. Ranariddh and Hun Sen formed an uneasy coalition after that poll.
Thai officials said they decided to allow the refugees in because they had nowhere to go and had to flee the fighting.
"They really needed to escape the fighting," one Thai official said.
Thai Army Major General Pravit Vongsuwan visited the makeshift refugee camps on the border and ordered soldiers and police to prevent any armed Cambodians from entering Thailand.
He said they would be disarmed before being allowed to cross the border.
Cambodian opposition leader Sam Rainsy told Reuters he had requested aid from the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR).

"We have urged UNHCR to send relief, and food and help with shelter as soon as possible," Rainsy said from Bangkok. He said he heard the number of refugees would rise as fighting had been going on in the border area for several days.

On Thursday government forces under Hun Sen took full control of Poipet after Ranariddh's men either defected to Hun Sen's side or withdrew to join their comrades in the jungle, officials in Poipet said.

The town, the main trading point on Cambodia's border with Thailand, has been tense since Ranariddh's ouster on July 6 and a brief clash between the rival forces on Sunday left four soldiers dead and eight wounded.

More than 15,000 displaced Cambodians who were unable to cross into Thailand further north at O'Samach, which borders Thailand's Surin province, received emergency food supplies from United Nations aid workers this week, the UNHCR said.
Sporadic battles have been going on in parts of Cambodia since a bloody July 5-6 power grab by Hun Sen in the capital Phnom Penh.
